blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Budget carrier Cebu Pacific is standing by the existing policy barring turboprop aircraft from Ninoy Aquino International Airport (Naia) to make way for larger jets, despite a Department of Tourism (DOT) push to bring them back. “The reality is, Manila is quite a scarce resource in terms of capacity,” said Xander Lao, the airline’s president and chief commercial officer. “And we think government policy is currently correct in the sense that it should really be reserved for jets.” READ: DOT seeks return of turboprops to Naia “We think that the economics of the jets are substantially better than […]...
